meta.rule: Only this file defines the current architecture. Archived proposals are non-authoritative.

purpose: Reliable, goal-bound, evidence-calibrated, method-adaptive, self-correcting cognition under explicit risk/resource/stop constraints.

core.responsibility: Understand target; construct a testable and revisable problem representation; choose suitable methods; generate a checkable result; validate/correct/reframe; stop or hand off honestly.
non_goals: Tools, roles, plugins, runtime, memory, governance and evaluation are support mechanisms, not parallel cognition cores.
Five-axis/nine-responsibility summaries are views only; no second skeleton or duplicate IDs.
No fixed full-path execution for all tasks.
No architecture component is immune to ablation, simplification, rejection or retirement.

axes.name: INTENT_AND_PROBLEM_FRAMING
axes.responsibility: Target, success criteria, scope, constraints, ambiguity, initial/alternative frames.

axes.name: EVIDENCE_AND_KNOWLEDGE_STATE
axes.responsibility: Source, observation, claim-evidence links, unknowns, conflicts, stale/unverified states.

axes.name: PROBLEM_MODEL_AND_EXPLANATION
axes.responsibility: Objects, relations, dependencies, causal candidates, competing hypotheses and discriminating tests.

axes.name: METHOD_AND_STRATEGY
axes.responsibility: Task profile, method routing, alternatives, risk/resource budget, next-step and stop rules.

axes.name: SOLVE_AND_FORM_RESULT
axes.responsibility: Execute the selected reasoning/research/design/engineering method; produce checkable outputs.

axes.name: VALIDATE_REFRAME_FEEDBACK
axes.responsibility: Check acceptance criteria, classify failure, correct/reframe, regress and close out.

invariants.observable: Target, acceptance criteria, hard constraints and non-goals are traceable.
Counterevidence can change the frame; alternatives/unknowns remain visible.
Source, observation, claim, inference, assumption, unknown, conflict and stale states are separate.
Method choice matches problem properties, observability, risk and budget.
Checks distinguish relevant alternatives; repetition is not independent evidence.
Conclusion strength and scope do not exceed the evidence.
Upstream changes identify and revalidate affected downstream outputs.
Tool success, text generation and task acceptance have separate states.
Authorization is enforced at runtime/tool boundary, not granted by routing.
Continue/stop considers marginal information value, remaining risk and cost.
Not-run, unverified, blocked, partial, failed and passed are not conflated.
Candidate components can be ablated, simplified, rejected or retired.

axes.question: How much analytical/method depth is needed?
How much state must persist for continuation/recovery/handoff?
How is work divided, delegated and integrated?

routing.orthogonality: M/G/P/T are independent dimensions; task type is a profile/tag, not a fifth axis.

profiles.when: Low ambiguity/risk, short task, easy acceptance.
profiles.minimum: Understand target, honor constraints, perform necessary check, deliver.

profiles.when: Ordinary analysis/planning with bounded uncertainty or multiple required steps.
profiles.minimum: Frame, track key evidence states, choose method, perform necessary validation.

profiles.when: High impact, critical unknown, conflicting sources, long dependencies or irreversible action.
profiles.minimum: Traceable dependencies, discriminating/independent validation, policy gate, authorization and recovery plan when applicable.

routing.permissions: Routing/profile selection never grants action permission. G/policy gate may block any M/P/T path.

persistence.P0: No additional persistence beyond the minimum explicitly required.
persistence.P1: Minimal traceable status, key outcomes, blockers and evidence references.
persistence.P2: Task-bound state bundle/checkpoint for multi-stage, cross-session, high-impact or interruptible work.

rules: Missing required evidence, scope or authorization must not be silently accepted.
Unknown external side effects require a distinct state and recovery decision.
An execution receipt is not the same as result-quality acceptance.
A document rule does not imply automated Runtime enforcement.

gate: Current blueprint and relevant IDs checked
Acceptance criteria/baseline/stop and rollback criteria fixed
Actual changes and execution receipts retained
Relevant regression and failure paths checked
Frozen version evaluated against predefined cases/thresholds
Independent or held-out checks used where applicable
Failures/unknowns preserved; pass only on actual evidence

delivery_lifecycle.invalidation: A change to target, core architecture, dependencies, acceptance criteria or relevant assumptions returns the affected scope to PLANNING and invalidates affected prior evidence.
